results.note: Rule 1: HEAD is appended last instead of inserted at the front, so on a score tie the oldest candidate wins the `[0]` pick rather than HEAD.
Rule 1 guard removed: a single-commit history where HEAD is the only candidate is no longer refused, so adoption is mistaken for a real sync point.
Rule 2: an exact-ours candidate that also equals theirs no longer short-circuits, so a proof-not-guess base is dropped into the scoring contest.
Rule 3 exemption keys off the wrong side: theirs-equal candidates lose their phantom immunity and the true base is rejected whenever live deleted >= 3 lines.
Rule 3 tie-break inverted: on an exact distance tie the theirs-equal candidate now wins by unearned immunity instead of losing.
Rule 4 removed: a phantom-rejected nearest candidate is returned as the base instead of refusing, turning refusals into silent wrong-base merges.
Rule 5 and/or swap: a single deleted line theirs happens to retain now rejects the candidate, refusing valid bases wholesale.
Phantom ratio counts `replace` opcodes too, so our own ${CLAUDE_USER_DIR} rewrites inflate the ratio and a true ancestor gets rejected.
Dropped EOL normalization on the ours comparison: a CRLF-vs-LF live file is misreported as two-sided instead of checkout-ahead.
or/and flip: a path that git cannot show falls through to infer_base with empty `theirs` instead of reporting `local snap`.
Direction block: collect now skips live-ahead files (the ones it should collect) and collects checkout-ahead files, undoing the other machine's work.
_print_file_diff drops EOL normalization, so a CRLF-vs-LF identical file prints a whole-file diff and exits 1 instead of reporting identical and exiting 0.
